entries.name: parse_electricity_ref
entries.doc:
Parses a Pakistani electricity bill identifier: a DISCO reference number,
a DISCO customer ID or a K-Electric account number.

PITC's bill pages take a 14-digit reference number with a separate U/R
choice, or a 10-digit customer ID (11 digits for LESCO); K-Electric asks for
a 13-digit account number starting with `04000`. No check digit is
published, so only the format is checked. Spaces, dashes and dots are
ignored, and Urdu digits are accepted. See DATA.md in the repository.

Returns `None` if the input matches none of the formats. Never raises.

entries.doc:
Validates a gas bill consumer number: 11 digits for SNGPL, 10 digits for
SSGC, as their bill pages ask for. No check digit is published, so only the
format is checked. `company` is `SNGPL` or `SSGC` (any case); anything
else returns `False`. Never raises. See DATA.md in the repository.

entries.name: find_cnics
entries.signature: def find_cnics(text: Any, *, across_lines: Any = False) -> List[CNICMatch]
entries.doc:
Finds CNIC numbers in free text, such as a chat message, a note or an
uploaded document, for example to mask them before logging.

Digits are read in groups (unbroken runs of digits). Groups may be
joined by any run of spaces or tabs, or by one mark (a hyphen or Unicode
dash, a dot, a slash or an underscore) with any spaces around it:
`35202 1234567 1`, `35202  1234567  1`, `35202 -1234567- 1`,
`35202_1234567_1`, `35202 - 1234567 - 1`, `352 0212 3456 71`,
`35202/1234567/1`. A line break never joins groups. A match is
consecutive whole groups that add up to exactly 13 digits, starting with
a province code (1-8); the search goes on after each match, so
`0300-1234567 35202-1234567-1` finds the CNIC. A group is never split,
so 13 digits inside a longer unbroken number (an IBAN, a card number)
never match. Digits may be ASCII, Urdu or Arabic-Indic, even mixed. This
matches everything Jaanch's own CNIC redaction does, except across line
breaks.

With `across_lines=True`, a single line break (`\r\n`, `\r` or
`\n`, with any spaces around it) also joins groups, as if it were a
space, so a CNIC written over several lines is found; a blank line (two
or more line breaks) never joins them. This can also join numbers on
consecutive lines, such as a list of amounts. Only `True` turns it on.

Accepting any grouping catches CNICs as people really type them, but
matches more that is not a CNIC: any 13 digits starting with 1-8 split
into groups this way (an account, order or tracking number, table
columns, a price list such as `8260 - 8048 - 2804 - 0`, a file name
such as `IMG_20261123_12345`, or two shorter numbers written together)
are found. {@link validate_cnic} stays strict.

`start` and `end` are Python string indexes (code points); the npm
package counts UTF-16 code units, which differ only after a character
outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as an emoji.

Returns the matches in order, or `[]` (also for a value that is not a
string). Never raises.

```python
>>> find_cnics("CNIC: 35202-1234567-1, phone 0300-1234567")
[CNICMatch(raw='35202-1234567-1', digits='3520212345671', formatted='35202-1234567-1', start=6, end=21)]
>>> find_cnics("id 352 0212 3456 71")[0].digits
'3520212345671'
>>> find_cnics("CNIC\n35202\n1234567\n1", across_lines=True)[0].formatted
'35202-1234567-1'
```

entries.name: mask_cnics
entries.signature:
def mask_cnics(
    text: Any,
    *,
    mask: Any = 'X',
    replacement: Any = None,
    across_lines: Any = False,
) -> MaskedText
entries.doc:
Masks every CNIC in free text, as found by {@link find_cnics}: each
digit becomes `mask` and the separators stay, so `35202-1234567-1`
becomes `XXXXX-XXXXXXX-X`. The rest of the text is unchanged.

With `replacement`, each whole CNIC, separators included, is replaced
by that string instead (e.g. `"[CNIC removed]"`). It takes precedence
over `mask`; a value that is not a string is ignored.

Like {@link find_cnics}, it also masks any other 13 digits that start
with 1-8, however they are grouped. `mask` is the string that replaces
each digit (default `"X"`; a value that is not a string means `"X"`).

With `across_lines=True`, CNICs written across single line breaks are
found too, as in {@link find_cnics}. With `mask` the line breaks stay;
with `replacement` they are replaced with the rest of the CNIC.

Returns the masked text and the number of CNICs masked. A value that is
not a string gives `MaskedText(text="", count=0)`. Never raises.

```python
>>> mask_cnics("My CNIC is 35202-1234567-1")
MaskedText(text='My CNIC is XXXXX-XXXXXXX-X', count=1)
>>> mask_cnics("35202 1234567 1", mask="*").text
'***** ******* *'
>>> mask_cnics("CNIC 352 0212 3456 71", replacement="[CNIC removed]").text
'CNIC [CNIC removed]'
```

modules.name: pakdatakit.courier
modules.doc:
Helpers for orders shipped with Pakistani couriers: status mapping and city names.

There are no API clients: nothing is sent anywhere.

entries.name: Courier
entries.doc: Couriers that {@link map_courier_status} knows about.

entries.name: CourierStatus
entries.doc: A courier's status in one vocabulary, from order to delivery or return. Experimental: the values may change in a minor release while more couriers' status lists are added.

entries.name: map_courier_status
entries.signature: def map_courier_status(courier: str, raw: Any) -> Optional[CourierStatus]
entries.doc:
Maps a courier's own status (its name, numeric ID or code, as the
courier documents it) to a {@link CourierStatus}.

Matching ignores case and extra spaces. PostEx's "Attempt Made: <reason>"
history messages map to `attempted`. `raw` is a string or a
non-negative integer (`5` and `5.0` are the same as `"5"`).

Only statuses the courier documents publicly are mapped: PostEx's API
guide and one Leopards status. TCS, M&P, Trax and BlueEx publish no list,
so they always return `None`, as does any status not in the list. No API
is called.

`courier` is `TCS`, `Leopards`, `PostEx`, `M&P`, `Trax` or
`BlueEx` (case-insensitive; `LCS`, `MnP` and `Blue Ex` are
accepted). Returns the status, or `None`. Never raises.

Experimental: only PostEx and one Leopards status are mapped so far. The
mapping and the {@link CourierStatus} values may change in a minor
release as other couriers' lists are added.

entries.name: normalize_city_for_courier
entries.doc:
Maps the way a customer or a courier writes a city to the city's name in
pakdatakit's city list, so orders can be matched against a courier's
service list.

Accepts the exact name in any case, short forms (`LHR`, `Khi`,
`Pindi`, `Isb`, `FSD`), the old name Lyallpur, a trailing "city", and
the main cities in Urdu script.

```python
>>> normalize_city_for_courier("LHR")
'Lahore'
>>> normalize_city_for_courier("Karachi City")
'Karachi'
>>> normalize_city_for_courier("Atlantis") is None
True
```

Returns a city from the city list, or `None`. Never raises.

modules.name: pakdatakit.fbr_invoice
modules.doc:
FBR Digital Invoicing (DI): types for the invoice JSON that is posted to
PRAL's gateway, a builder that works out the sales tax, and an offline
validator for the rules that can be checked without FBR's reference APIs.

Built from PRAL's "Technical Specification for DI API", version 1.12 (last
updated 24 July 2025), and PRAL's "Error Message Guide (Sales)"; see DATA.md.
Nothing here talks to FBR: there is no HTTP client and no token handling.
Values that only FBR's reference APIs can confirm (provinces, HS codes, units,
rates, sale types, SRO numbers) are checked for presence, not against FBR's
lists, unless the app passes the lists it synced from those APIs
(`validate_fbr_invoice(invoice, reference=...)`).

The invoice is a plain `dict` with the camelCase keys FBR expects, so it can
be sent with `json.dumps` as is. The `TypedDict` classes below describe it.

entries.doc: Version of PRAL's technical specification this module follows.

entries.doc: `invoiceType` values in the specification.

entries.name: FbrInvoiceReference

Reference lists from FBR's own APIs (PRAL's `/pdi/v1/provinces`,

`/pdi/v2/SaleTypeToRate` ...), which an app syncs with its token. FBR's

entries.doc:
A sale type as PRAL's specification names it, with its sandbox
scenarios. Returned by {@link get_sale_types}.

fields.doc: The specification's sandbox scenarios (SN001-SN028) that use it.

entries.name: get_sale_types
entries.doc:
The sale types named in PRAL's DI specification (v1.12, section 9,
"Scenarios for Sandbox Testing"), with the scenarios that use each.

FBR's full, current list comes from its reference API; this is a
convenience for building forms and tests, and {@link validate_fbr_invoice}
does not reject a sale type that is not in it.

```python
>>> get_sale_types()[0]
FbrSaleType(sale_type='Goods at Standard Rate (default)', scenario_ids=['SN001', 'SN002', 'SN026'])
```

entries.name: expected_sales_tax
entries.doc:
The sales tax FBR expects on a line, in rupees, or `None` when the
rate is not a plain percentage or per-unit amount (spec 7, errors 0102,
0104, 0105):

- `N%` on Third Schedule goods: retail price x rate (0102);
- `N%` otherwise: value excluding sales tax x rate (0104);
- `Rs.N`: quantity x N (0105).

Rounded half up to the paisa (the specification allows 2 decimals and
gives no rounding rule). `item` is a `dict` with FBR's camelCase keys.
Never raises.

```python
>>> expected_sales_tax({"rate": "18%", "valueSalesExcludingST": 1234})
222.12
>>> expected_sales_tax({"rate": "Rs.3", "quantity": 12})
36.0
```

entries.name: build_fbr_invoice
entries.doc:
Builds an FBR digital invoice from your own fields, working out
`salesTaxApplicable` on each line where you leave it out (see
{@link expected_sales_tax}; uses {@link calculate_sales_tax}). Lines with
a rate that is neither `N%` nor `Rs.N` (`Exempt`, combined rates)
get 0 unless you give the tax.

`input` is a `dict` with FBR's camelCase keys (see
{@link FbrInvoiceInput}). `salesTaxWithheldAtSource`, `totalValues`
and `fixedNotifiedValueOrRetailPrice` default to 0, and
`invoiceRefNo` and `buyerNTNCNIC` to `""`, as in FBR's samples.
Nothing else is filled in or changed (other keys are kept); check the
result with {@link validate_fbr_invoice}.

Also returns column totals, which are for your own records: the
specification has no invoice-level totals.

Returns {@link FbrInvoiceBuild} (`invoice`, `totals`), or `None`
if `input` is not a `dict` with an `items` list of `dict` items.
Never raises.

entries.name: validate_fbr_invoice
entries.doc:
Checks an FBR digital invoice against the rules of PRAL's specification
(v1.12) and Error Message Guide that need no call to FBR, and returns
every problem with FBR's error code.

Checked: invoice type (0003, 0011), date format (0005, 0042, 0113) and,
with `today` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), a future date (0043); seller and buyer
NTN/CNIC (0401, 0402, 0009), self-invoicing (0058), names, provinces
(0073, 0074), addresses, buyer registration type (0012), the reference
number of a debit note (0026), the sandbox scenario, and on each line: HS
code (0044), rate (0020), unit, sale type (0013), required and valid
amounts (0021, 0023, 0024, 0098, 0300, 0302), SRO schedule and serial
(0077, 0078), Third Schedule retail price (0090), extra tax on
reduced-rate goods (0091) and the sales tax arithmetic (0102, 0104, 0105,
to within one paisa).

Not checked, because they need FBR's data: registration status, whether a
province, HS code, unit, rate, sale type or SRO is in FBR's lists or fits
the others, and the original invoice of a debit note.

Pass the lists your app syncs from FBR's reference APIs as `reference`
(a {@link FbrInvoiceReference} `dict`: `provinces`, `saleTypes`,
`uoms`, `hsUom`; the snake_case keys `sale_types` and `hs_uom`
work too) to check them: provinces (0073, 0074), sale types (0013), units
(0099) and, with `hsUom`, that each HS code is listed (no code) and the
unit is allowed for it (0099). Matching ignores case and extra spaces.
Lists left out, or not given as lists, are not checked; FBR's APIs are
authoritative.

`invoice` is a `dict` with FBR's camelCase keys; any value (untrusted
JSON) is accepted. Returns {@link FbrInvoiceValidation} (`valid`,
`errors`). Never raises.

modules.name: pakdatakit.format
modules.doc: Pakistani Rupee and lakh/crore formatting.

entries.name: format_pkr
entries.doc:
Formats an amount as `"Rs. 150,000"`, rounded to whole rupees.

Raises `ValueError` if `amount` is NaN or infinite.

entries.name: format_lakh
entries.doc:
Formats an amount with lakh/crore units (`"25 Lakh"`, `"1 Crore"`).

Values are rounded to two decimals before the unit is chosen, so
`9999999` renders as `"1 Crore"`. Smaller amounts fall back to
{@link format_pkr}. Raises `ValueError` if `amount` is NaN or infinite.

entries.name: ParsedAmount
entries.doc: Result of {@link parse_amount}.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The amount in rupees, rounded half-up to the paisa (2 decimals).

fields.name: raw
fields.doc: The input with surrounding whitespace removed.

entries.name: parse_amount
entries.doc:
Reads a rupee amount the way people type it in Pakistan, and returns it
in rupees, rounded half-up to the paisa. Returns `None` for anything that
is not exactly one non-negative amount; it never raises.

Accepted:

- digits, with or without grouping: `150000`, `150,000`
  (international) or `1,50,000` (Pakistani: groups of two, then three),
  and decimals (`1,234.50`, `.5`, `5.`); a grouping must be complete
  and consistent;
- Urdu (`۱۵۰۰۰۰`) and Arabic-Indic (`١٥٠٠٠٠`) digits, also
  mixed with 0-9, and the Arabic decimal and thousands separators
  (`٫`, `٬`);
- one currency mark before or after the number: `Rs`, `Rs.`, `PKR`
  or `₨` (any case), and a trailing `/-` (`Rs. 5,000/-`);
- one shorthand unit after the number, with or without a space, in any
  case: `k`, `thousand(s)`, `hazar`, `ہزار` (x 1,000); `lakh(s)`,
  `lac(s)`, `لاکھ` (x 100,000); `crore(s)`, `cr`, `کروڑ`
  (x 10,000,000). Decimals work with units: `1.5 lakh` is 150,000 and
  `2.25cr` is 22,500,000;
- whitespace around and between the parts (spaces, tabs, line breaks and
  no-break spaces).

Rejected (`None`): non-string or empty input, negative or signed amounts
(`-500`, `+500`), ranges (`5-10k`), more than one number
(`500 600`), two currency marks or two units, leftover letters
(`500 rupees`, `5kk`), grouping that could be read two ways or is
broken (`1,50`, `1.500,00`, `1,5000`), and amounts over Rs. 50
trillion (50 lakh crore), beyond which a float can no longer hold every
paisa exactly.

The arithmetic is done on the digits, so the result is exact: `1.005`
rounds to 1.01 and `1.5 lakh` is exactly 150000.

```python
>>> parse_amount("Rs. 1,50,000/-")
ParsedAmount(value=150000.0, raw='Rs. 1,50,000/-')
>>> parse_amount("2.25cr")
ParsedAmount(value=22500000.0, raw='2.25cr')
>>> parse_amount("5-10k") is None
True
```

entries.name: format_amount_input
entries.doc:
Writes back an amount typed in any form {@link parse_amount} accepts,
for showing next to the field ("= Rs. 150,000"): `Rs.`, international
grouping, and paisa only when there are any (`Rs. 1,234.50`). Returns
`None` when {@link parse_amount} does; it never raises.

```python
>>> format_amount_input("1.5 lakh")
'Rs. 150,000'
```

Returns the administrative divisions of Pakistan, or of one province, sorted.

The list is the 30 divisions of the 2023 census: Punjab 9, Sindh 6, Khyber
Pakhtunkhwa 7 and Balochistan 8. Islamabad has no division, and the census
tables do not cover Azad Jammu and Kashmir or Gilgit-Baltistan. Divisions
created since the census (such as Gujrat in Punjab) are not included.

`province` is case-insensitive; leave it out for all divisions.

entries.doc:
Returns the division a district belonged to in the 2023 census, or `None`.

Census-district caveat: only the 136 districts of the 2023 census have a
division here, under the name they had then (so `Quetta`, `Dera Bugti`
and `South Waziristan` work, and their successors do not). Districts
created after the census, and those of Azad Jammu and Kashmir,
Gilgit-Baltistan and Islamabad, return `None`.

Returns the tehsils (talukas, sub-divisions) of a district, sorted.

Census-district caveat: the data is the 591 tehsil-level units of the 2023
census, each recorded under the district it was in then. For a district of
the 2023 census this returns its census tehsils, even if some have since
moved to a new district (so `Rawalpindi` still lists Murree). For a
district created after the census it returns only the tehsils an official
source places in it, which can be an empty list. Azad Jammu and Kashmir
and Gilgit-Baltistan are not covered.

`district` is case-insensitive; former names such as `Quetta` and
`South Waziristan` work.

entries.name: get_tehsil_district
entries.doc:
Returns the district a tehsil was in at the 2023 census, or `None`.

Census-district caveat: the result is the census district, which may have
been split since (a tehsil of `Quetta` is now in Quetta East or Quetta
West). A few names are shared by tehsils in different districts
(`Saddar`, `Sahiwal`, `Khanpur`); pass the province to tell them
apart. Returns `None` when the name is unknown or still matches more
than one district.

modules.name: pakdatakit.incometax
modules.doc: Income tax on salary in Pakistan, from the salaried rate table.

entries.name: SalaryTaxSlab
entries.doc:
One band of the salaried rate table: income above `over` (and up to
`up_to`) pays `fixed` plus `rate` percent of the amount above `over`.

fields.name: over
fields.doc: Lower bound in rupees (income must exceed it).

fields.name: up_to
fields.doc: Upper bound in rupees, or `None` for the top band.

fields.name: fixed
fields.doc: Tax on the income up to `over`, in rupees.

fields.name: rate
fields.doc: Percent of the income above `over`.

entries.name: SalaryTaxSurcharge
entries.doc:
The surcharge under section 4AB of the Income Tax Ordinance: `rate`
percent of the tax from the rate table, payable when taxable income exceeds
`over` rupees.

fields.name: rate
fields.doc: Percent of the tax from the rate table. `0` where the law sets none.

fields.name: over
fields.doc: Taxable income must exceed this many rupees (Rs 10 million).

fields.name: law
fields.doc: The law that sets it.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Official document.

entries.name: SalaryTaxYear
entries.doc: The salaried rate table for one tax year (1 July to 30 June).

fields.name: tax_year
fields.doc: The tax year, named after the June it ends in: 2026 is 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026.

fields.name: from_
fields.doc: `YYYY-MM-DD`, always 1 July. (`from` in the npm package; `from_` because `from` is a keyword.)

fields.name: to
fields.doc: `YYYY-MM-DD`, always 30 June.

fields.name: law
fields.doc: The law that sets the table.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Official document.

fields.name: surcharge
fields.doc: The section 4AB surcharge on salaried individuals for the year, or `None` for years before it existed (tax years up to 2024).

entries.name: SalaryTax
entries.doc: Result of {@link calculate_salary_tax} and {@link calculate_monthly_salary_tax}.

fields.name: tax
fields.doc: Tax for the year from the rate table, in rupees, rounded half up to the paisa.

fields.name: surcharge
fields.doc: The section 4AB surcharge, rounded half up to the paisa. `0` unless `include_surcharge` is set and the year and income attract one.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: `tax + surcharge`: the year's total.

fields.name: monthly
fields.doc: `total / 12`, rounded half up to the paisa.

fields.name: effective_rate
fields.doc: `total` as a percent of the income, rounded half up to 2 decimals.

fields.name: slab
fields.doc: The band the income falls in.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: The rate table used: its tax year's dates, law and official source.

entries.name: get_tax_year
entries.doc:
The tax year (July to June) that contains a date, or `None` for an
invalid date.

`date` is `YYYY-MM-DD` or a `datetime.date`, and defaults to today's
local date. Never raises.

```python
>>> get_tax_year("2025-07-01")
2026
```

entries.name: get_salary_tax_slabs
entries.doc:
Returns the salaried rate table for a tax year: Division I of Part I of
the First Schedule to the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, clause (2), which
applies when salary is more than 75% of taxable income.

Covers tax years 2020 to 2027, each from FBR's consolidated Ordinance.
`tax_year` is e.g. `2026` (1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026) and defaults to
the current tax year. Returns `None` for a year that is not covered.
Never raises.

entries.name: get_salary_tax_years
entries.doc: Which tax years {@link get_salary_tax_slabs} covers, oldest first.

entries.name: calculate_salary_tax
entries.signature:
def calculate_salary_tax(
    annual_income: Any,
    *,
    tax_year: Any = None,
    date: Any = None,
    include_surcharge: bool = False,
) -> Optional[SalaryTax]
entries.doc:
Income tax on a salaried individual's taxable income for a tax year,
from the salaried rate table (see {@link get_salary_tax_slabs}).

`annual_income` is the taxable income for the year in rupees, 0 to 1
trillion (at most 2 decimals count). `tax_year` (e.g. `2026`) takes
precedence over `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD` or a `datetime.date`, a day in
the tax year); with neither, the current tax year is used.

With `include_surcharge=True` it adds the section 4AB surcharge: a
percentage of the whole tax once taxable income exceeds Rs 10 million (10%
in tax year 2025, 9% for salaried individuals in 2026, none in 2027 or
before 2025). Because it applies to the whole tax, one rupee over Rs 10
million adds it in full. It is off by default in 2.x so that existing
results do not change, and will be on by default in 3.0.

Tax credits, exemptions, the separate pension rate, super tax and
withholding adjustments are not applied. This is an estimate, not tax
advice. `source` gives the rate table's dates, law and official
document (a {@link DataSource}). Returns `None` for an invalid amount
or a tax year that is not covered. Never raises.

```python
>>> calculate_salary_tax(1_800_000, tax_year=2026).tax
72000.0
>>> calculate_salary_tax(12_000_000, tax_year=2026, include_surcharge=True).total
3685290.0
```

entries.name: calculate_monthly_salary_tax
entries.signature:
def calculate_monthly_salary_tax(
    monthly_salary: Any,
    *,
    tax_year: Any = None,
    date: Any = None,
    include_surcharge: bool = False,
) -> Optional[SalaryTax]
entries.doc:
{@link calculate_salary_tax} for a monthly salary: the income is
`monthly_salary * 12`, and `monthly` is the tax to withhold each month.
`include_surcharge` adds the section 4AB surcharge, as there.

```python
>>> calculate_monthly_salary_tax(150_000, tax_year=2026).monthly
6000.0
```

entries.doc:
Identifies and formats any Pakistani telephone number.

Handles mobile, landline, UAN (`111`), toll-free (`0800`) and
premium-rate (`0900`) numbers. 0122 numbers are not recognised: no PTA
document lists them (see DATA.md). Returns `None` if invalid.

entries.name: validate_landline
entries.signature: def validate_landline(phone: str, *, services: bool = False) -> bool
entries.doc:
Validates a Pakistani landline (fixed-line) number such as `042-35761234`.

With `services=True` it also accepts the non-geographic service numbers a
business may give as its landline: UAN (`021-111-123-456`,
`111-123-456`), toll-free (`0800-12345`) and premium rate
(`0900-12345`); {@link analyze_number} tells them apart with its `type`
field. Returns `False` for a value that is not a string. Never raises.

```python
>>> validate_landline("042-35761234")
True
>>> validate_landline("021-111-123-456")
False
>>> validate_landline("021-111-123-456", services=True)
True
```

A district's population, households and urban/rural split from
Pakistan's 2023 census (Pakistan Bureau of Statistics), for any of the
177 districts in {@link get_districts_by_province}.

- Districts created after the census have `None` figures and name the
  census district their area was part of; nothing is estimated.
- Districts that lost area to a new district keep their census figures,
  with `boundary_changed=True`.
- Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir were not enumerated by this
  census, so their figures are `None`.

their source, or `None` for an unknown district or a value that is not
a string. Never raises.

>>> get_district_population("Lahore").population
13004135

True

urban/rural split from the 2023 census, for the 591 units in the census

one district; give `district` (the district at the census or today) to
choose. Returns the figures and their source, or `None` for an unknown
or ambiguous name or a value that is not a string. Never raises.

```python
>>> get_tehsil_population("Murree").current_district
'Murree'
```

entries.doc:
Returns the city for a Pakistani postal code (whitespace is ignored), or `None`.

Only codes of post offices in a city on pakdatakit's city list return a
city (`54660` -> `Lahore`). The code of a post office in a town or
village that is not on the list returns `None`; use
{@link get_post_office} for those.

entries.name: get_postal_code
entries.doc: Returns the primary (GPO) postal code for a city, or `None`.

entries.name: get_postal_codes
entries.doc: Returns all known postal codes for a city, sorted.

entries.name: search_postal_codes
entries.doc: Searches postal entries by city name, area, or postal code prefix.

entries.name: get_postal_areas
entries.doc: Returns known area names for a city's postal entries, sorted.

entries.doc: A delivery post office from Pakistan Post's post code directory.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: 5-digit post code, e.g. `48330`.

fields.name: office
fields.doc: Office name as the directory gives it, in title case, e.g. `Dulmial`.

fields.name: town
fields.doc: The city the office belongs to when that is known (`Lahore` for an office in Lahore); otherwise the office's own name, which for most offices is its town or village.

fields.name: district

fields.name: province

entries.name: get_post_office
entries.doc:
Returns the delivery post office for a post code, from Pakistan Post's
directory of about 2,560 offices.

Unlike {@link get_city_by_postal_code}, which only answers for codes in
the cities pakdatakit lists, this knows every delivery office, including
those in towns and villages. Whitespace in `code` is ignored.

Returns `None` if the code is not in the directory.

```python
>>> get_post_office("48330")
PostOffice(code='48330', office='Dulmial', town='Dulmial', district=None, province='Punjab')
```

entries.name: search_post_offices
entries.doc:
Searches Pakistan Post's directory by office name, town or post code.

Matching is case-insensitive: an office matches when its name or town
contains the query, or its code starts with it. Returns the matching post
offices, sorted by post code.

entries.doc:
Scores how complete a free-form Pakistani delivery address is, for cash
on delivery and other courier use.

Built on {@link parse_address}. It looks for a city, a house, plot or flat
number, a street, an area, a postal code and a landmark ("near", "opp",
"nazd", "qareeb", "سامنے" ...), and adds up {@link ADDRESS_WEIGHTS}. A
postal code that is a known post office raises the score more than an
unknown one, and a post office in a different province from the city
lowers it (with a warning in `parsed.warnings`).

This is a heuristic: it says how much an address tells a rider, not
whether the address exists. It never raises.

```python
>>> score_address("House 12, Street 4, Block B, Gulberg III, near Liberty Market, Lahore 54660").score
100
```

entries.name: PhoneRiskFlag
entries.doc: A reason to double-check a phone number given for a delivery.

entries.name: phone_risk_signals
entries.doc:
Flags a phone number that a courier cannot reach by SMS or call, or
that looks made up. Pure heuristics on the number itself: no list of real
numbers, no personal data, no network call.

- `invalid`: not a Pakistani phone number.
- `landline`: a fixed-line number (no SMS, often unanswered).
- `not-mobile`: a UAN, toll-free or other service number.
- `repeated-digits`: the 7-digit subscriber part uses at most two
  different digits (`0300-0000000`, `0300-1111112`).
- `sequential-digits`: the subscriber part is a run such as `1234567`
  or `7654321`.
- `test-number`: a placeholder often typed into forms
  (`03XX-1234567`, `03XX-7654321`, `0312-3456789`).

A valid mobile number with nothing suspicious returns `[]`. It never
raises.

```python
>>> phone_risk_signals("03001234567")
['sequential-digits', 'test-number']
```

modules.name: pakdatakit.raast
modules.doc:
Raast QR codes: SBP person-to-person and EMVCo merchant QR payloads.

Implements SBP's "Standard for Interoperable QR Code for Person-to-Person and
Merchant Payments" v1.0 (DI&SD Circular Letter No. 1 of 2022, Annex-I).

entries.doc: A parsed EMV field. `children` is set for template fields.

entries.name: MerchantAccountInfo
entries.doc: Account details for a merchant QR, as issued by the merchant's bank.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: Sub-fields of the template, keyed by 2-digit ID, in the order given.

fields.name: tag
fields.doc: Template tag. SBP reserves `28`-`30` for Raast. Defaults to `28`.

entries.name: ParsedRaastQr
entries.doc: Result of {@link parse_raast_qr}.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: `"p2p"` for person-to-person QR codes, `"merchant"` for EMVCo merchant QR codes.

fields.name: dynamic
fields.doc: Whether the QR carries a fixed amount (point of initiation 12).

fields.name: crc_valid
fields.doc: Whether the CRC checksum matches.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: P2P: expiry of a dynamic QR as local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`.

fields.name: due_date
fields.doc: Due date as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: All top-level fields, with template fields parsed into `children`.

entries.name: RaastQrValidation
entries.doc: Result of {@link validate_raast_qr}.

fields.name: valid
fields.doc: `True` when there are no errors.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: `p2p` for a person-to-person QR, `merchant` for a merchant QR, `None` when the text is not a Raast QR.

fields.name: errors
fields.doc: `not-a-raast-qr`, `bad-checksum`, `no-iban`, `invalid-iban`, `expired` or `missing-expiry`.

fields.name: warnings
fields.doc: `amount-ignored`, `expires-soon` or `no-iban` (a merchant QR that names no IBAN: it pays through the merchant's own scheme, so the payee can't be checked from the QR).

fields.name: qr
fields.doc: The parsed QR, or `None` if it could not be read.

entries.name: create_raast_p2p_qr
entries.signature:
def create_raast_p2p_qr(
    iban: str,
    *,
    amount: Optional[Number] = None,
    expires_at: Optional[_dt.datetime] = None,
    expires_in: Optional[Duration] = None,
    bank_name: Optional[str] = None,
    particulars: Optional[str] = None,
    scheme: Optional[str] = _DEFAULT_P2P_SCHEME,
    now: Optional[_dt.datetime] = None,
) -> str
entries.doc:
Creates a Raast person-to-person QR payload (SBP P2P format `02`).

Matches the QR codes banking apps generate, so Easypaisa, JazzCash and
other apps can scan it. Encode the returned string with any QR library.

A QR with an `amount` is dynamic and needs `expires_at` (a naive local
`datetime`) or `expires_in` (milliseconds, a `timedelta`, or a string
such as `"30m"`, `"12h"` or `"7d"`, counted from `now`, which
defaults to the current local time).

Raises `ValueError` if the IBAN is invalid, a field is too long, or an
amount is given without an expiry.

entries.name: create_merchant_qr
entries.signature:
def create_merchant_qr(
    merchant_account: Union[MerchantAccountInfo, Mapping[str, Any]],
    merchant_name: str,
    city: str,
    *,
    mcc: Optional[str] = None,
    amount: Optional[Number] = None,
    dynamic: Optional[bool] = None,
    bill_number: Optional[str] = None,
    mobile_number: Optional[str] = None,
    reference: Optional[str] = None,
    due_date: Optional[_dt.date] = None,
    amount_after_due_date: Optional[Number] = None,
) -> str
entries.doc:
Creates an EMVCo merchant-presented QR payload per SBP's Pakistan QR standard.

`merchant_account` is a {@link MerchantAccountInfo} or a dict such as
`{"tag": "28", "fields": {"00": "A000000736", "01": iban}}` holding the
template sub-fields your bank gives you.

Raises `ValueError` if a field is missing, too long, or out of range.

entries.name: parse_raast_qr
entries.doc:
Parses a Raast QR payload (P2P format `02` or EMVCo merchant format `01`)
and verifies its CRC. Returns `None` if it is not a well-formed Pakistani QR code.

entries.name: validate_raast_qr
entries.doc:
Checks whether a Raast QR code can be paid.

Errors: not a Pakistani payment QR, checksum mismatch, a person-to-person
QR with no IBAN, an invalid IBAN, expired, or a fixed-amount QR without an
expiry.
Warnings: an amount in a static QR (apps ignore it), a QR that expires
within `expires_soon_ms` (default one hour) of `now` (default: the
current local time), or a merchant QR with no IBAN (`no-iban`): merchant
QRs may pay through the merchant's own scheme, so it is valid, but the
payee can't be checked from the QR.

`kind` is `p2p`, `merchant`, or `None` when the text is not a
Raast QR.

fields.doc: Percent, e.g. `18`.

fields.doc: First day it applied (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Coverage starts on 1 July 2019. (`from` in the npm package; `from_` because `from` is a keyword.)

fields.doc: Value excluding tax (2 decimals at most).

fields.name: gross
fields.doc: Value including tax.

fields.name: rate
fields.doc: Percent used.

entries.name: get_sales_tax_rate
entries.doc:
Returns the standard sales tax rate for goods (federal, Sales Tax Act
1990) or for services in a province or Islamabad Capital Territory, on a
given date.

`kind` is `"goods"` or `"services"`. `province` (needed for
services) accepts the province names and `KP`, `KPK`, `ICT` and
`Islamabad`. `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD` or a `datetime.date`, and
defaults to today's local date.

Only standard rates are covered, from 1 July 2019. Reduced, higher and
sector rates are not. Returns `None` for an unknown province or kind, an
invalid date, a date before 1 July 2019, services without a province, or
goods in Azad Jammu and Kashmir or Gilgit-Baltistan. Never raises.

```python
>>> get_sales_tax_rate(kind="services", province="Sindh", date="2024-06-30").rate
13
```

entries.name: split_inclusive
entries.signature: def split_inclusive(gross: Any, rate: Any) -> Optional[SalesTaxAmounts]
entries.doc:
Splits an amount that includes sales tax into its value and tax.

The value is rounded half up to the paisa and the tax is the rest, so
`net + tax` is always `gross`. `gross` is 0 to 1 trillion rupees and
`rate` a percent from 0 to 100 with at most 2 decimals. Returns `None`
for an invalid amount or rate. Never raises.

```python
>>> split_inclusive(1180, 18)
SalesTaxAmounts(net=1000.0, tax=180.0, gross=1180.0, rate=18.0, source=None)
```

entries.name: calculate_sales_tax
entries.signature:
def calculate_sales_tax(
    amount: Any,
    *,
    rate: Any = None,
    province: Optional[str] = None,
    kind: Any = None,
    date: Any = None,
    inclusive: Any = False,
) -> Optional[SalesTaxAmounts]
entries.doc:
Adds sales tax to an amount, or splits it out when `inclusive=True`.

Give a `rate` (percent, 0 to 100, at most 2 decimals; it takes
precedence), or a `province` (and `kind`, default `"services"`, and
`date`) to use the standard rate from {@link get_sales_tax_rate}. The
tax is rounded half up to the paisa. `amount` is 0 to 1 trillion rupees.

When the rate was looked up, `source` gives its period, law and
official document (a {@link DataSource}); with your own `rate` it is
`None`.

Returns `None` if the amount, rate or province is invalid or no rate
applies. Never raises.

```python
>>> calculate_sales_tax(1000, rate=18)
SalesTaxAmounts(net=1000.0, tax=180.0, gross=1180.0, rate=18.0, source=None)
>>> calculate_sales_tax(1000, province="Punjab", date="2026-11-18").tax
160.0
>>> calculate_sales_tax(1000, province="Punjab", date="2026-11-18").source.effective_from
'2019-07-01'
```

modules.name: pakdatakit.text
modules.doc:
Text normalization, Roman Urdu spelling, Urdu digits, slugs, Urdu sorting
and bidirectional text.

entries.name: normalize_text
entries.doc: Trims, collapses whitespace and applies Unicode NFC.

entries.name: normalize_roman_urdu
entries.doc:
Normalizes informal Roman Urdu spellings (`kia` -> `kya`).

Also applies {@link normalize_text} and converts Urdu/Arabic digits to
English. A capitalized word keeps its capital; all-caps words are left alone.

entries.name: to_urdu_digits
entries.doc: Converts English and Arabic-Indic digits to Urdu digits (۰-۹).

entries.name: to_english_digits
entries.doc: Converts Urdu and Arabic-Indic digits to English digits (0-9).

entries.name: SlugScript
entries.doc: Which letters {@link slugify} keeps: `any` (Latin and Urdu), `latin` or `urdu`.

entries.name: BidiDirection
entries.doc: Direction for {@link wrap_bidi}.

entries.name: slugify
entries.signature: def slugify(text: Any, *, script: Any = 'any') -> str
entries.doc:
Turns text into a URL slug: lower-case words joined by `-`.

Urdu letters are kept as they are (no transliteration). Diacritics,
tatweel and zero-width characters are dropped, the Arabic look-alikes
ك ي ى become the Urdu ک ی ی, Urdu and Arabic-Indic digits become `0-9`,
and accented Latin-1 letters lose their accents (`é` -> `e`, `ß` ->
`ss`). Anything else separates words.

`script` is `"any"` (default: Latin and Urdu letters), `"latin"`
(only `a-z`) or `"urdu"` (only Urdu letters); any other value is
`"any"`. Digits are always kept.

Returns `""` when nothing is left or `text` is not a string. Never raises.

```python
>>> slugify("Lahore Fort, 2024")
'lahore-fort-2024'
>>> slugify("کراچی ۲۰۲۴", script="urdu")
'کراچی-2024'
```

entries.name: compare_urdu
entries.signature: def compare_urdu(a: Any, b: Any) -> int
entries.doc:
Compares two strings in Urdu alphabetical order; use with
`functools.cmp_to_key`.

Letters follow the Unicode CLDR collation for Urdu (`ur`, CLDR 49):
ا آ ب بھ پ پھ ت تھ ٹ ٹھ ث ج جھ چ چھ ح خ د دھ ڈ ڈھ ذ ر رھ ڑ ڑھ ز ژ س ش ص ض
ط ظ ع غ ف ق ک کھ گ گھ ل لھ م مھ ن نھ ں ںھ و وھ ہ ھ ۃ ء ی یھ ے. A letter
joined with ھ is a letter of its own. أ ؤ ۂ ئ ۓ sort as ا و ہ ی ے and come
just after them when words are otherwise equal, and diacritics only break
ties, in CLDR's order.

Outside the Urdu letters: spaces and punctuation come first, then digits
digit by digit (Urdu, Arabic-Indic and ASCII digits are equal; `10`
comes before `2`), then Urdu letters, then other Arabic-script
characters (the look-alikes ك ي ى ه ة), then everything else by code
point, ignoring ASCII case. Strings that are still equal are ordered by
code point, so the result is 0 only for identical strings.

Returns `-1`, `0` or `1`. A value that is not a string is treated as
`""`. Never raises.

```python
>>> from functools import cmp_to_key
>>> sorted(["ے", "بھائی", "آم", "باغ", "اب"], key=cmp_to_key(compare_urdu))
['اب', 'آم', 'باغ', 'بھائی', 'ے']
```

entries.name: is_rtl
entries.doc:
Whether text reads right to left: its first letter is from a
right-to-left script such as Urdu or Arabic. Digits, punctuation and
spaces are skipped, as in the Unicode bidirectional algorithm's paragraph
rule.

Returns `False` when there is no letter or `text` is not a string.
Never raises.

```python
>>> is_rtl("123 سلام")
True
>>> is_rtl("Order نمبر")
False
```

entries.name: wrap_bidi
entries.signature: def wrap_bidi(text: Any, direction: Any = 'auto') -> str
entries.doc:
Wraps text in Unicode directional isolates, so a name or number in one
direction does not reorder the sentence around it (for example an English
order number inside an Urdu message).

Uses FIRST STRONG ISOLATE (U+2068) by default, RIGHT-TO-LEFT ISOLATE
(U+2067) for `"rtl"` and LEFT-TO-RIGHT ISOLATE (U+2066) for `"ltr"`,
closed with POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE (U+2069). Any other direction is
`"auto"`.

Returns `""` when `text` is not a string. Never raises.

```python
>>> wrap_bidi("PDK-1042")
'\u2068PDK-1042\u2069'
```

entries.name: roman_urdu_key
entries.doc:
A phonetic key for Roman Urdu, so that different spellings of the same
name or word match: `Mubeen` and `Mobeen`, `Muhammad`, `Mohammad`
and `Muhammed`, `Rehman` and `Rahman`, `Chaudhry`, `Chaudhary`
and `Chaudhery`. Compare keys, not the text.

Each word keeps its consonants, its first vowel sound and a vowel sound at
its end. Letters for one sound are merged (`kh`, `sh`, `ch`; `ph`
and `f`; `q`, `c` and `k`; `v` and `w`; `th` and `t`,
`dh` and `d`), doubled letters count once, `e` counts as `a`,
`o` as `u`, and a final `h` after a vowel is dropped. Accents are
removed and anything other than Latin letters splits words. The key is not
meant to be shown: it is an opaque string.

Different names can share a key (`Hamid` and `Hamad`), so treat a match
as "probably the same", not proof. {@link normalize_roman_urdu} is a
different tool: it rewrites informal spellings into readable text.

Returns the key, one part per word separated by spaces; `""` for text
with no Latin letters or a value that is not a string. Never raises.

```python
>>> roman_urdu_key("Mubeen") == roman_urdu_key("Mobeen")
True
>>> roman_urdu_key("Muhammad Rehman")
'muhmd rahmn'
>>> roman_urdu_key("Hussain") == roman_urdu_key("Hassan")
False
```

entries.name: get_withholding_rates
entries.doc:
Every case FBR's Withholding Tax Rate Card lists for the covered
sections in a tax year (2025 to 2027), with its rates for persons on and
not on the Active Taxpayers List and its references.

`tax_year` is e.g. `2027`; `section` (optional, e.g. `"153"`, in
any case) keeps only that section. Returns the cases, or `[]` for a
year that is not covered. Never raises.

```python
>>> [r.sub_type for r in get_withholding_rates(2027, "236K")]
['purchase']
```

entries.name: calculate_withholding
entries.signature:
def calculate_withholding(
    input: Any = None,
    *,
    section: Any = None,
    sub_type: Any = None,
    amount: Any = None,
    atl: Any = None,
    late_filer: Any = False,
    return_on_investment: Any = None,
    resident: Any = None,
    tax_year: Any = None,
    date: Any = None,
) -> Optional[Withholding]
entries.doc:
Income tax to withhold or collect under one section of the Income Tax
Ordinance 2001, for a person on or not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List
(ATL), from FBR's Withholding Tax Rate Card for tax years 2025 to 2027.

Covered: 231AB cash withdrawal, 236C sale and 236K purchase of immovable
property, 151 profit on debt, 150 dividends, 153 goods, services and
contracts, 154B social media income (from 2027) and 149 salary (the
salaried rate table, as {@link calculate_salary_tax}).

`section` is the section (`"231AB"`, `"236C"`, `"236K"`,
`"151"`, `"150"`, `"153"`, `"154B"` or `"149"`, in any case);
`sub_type` the case, e.g. `"bank-deposit"` (151) or
`"goods-company"` (153), optional for sections with one case (see
{@link get_withholding_rates}). `amount` is the payment (for 236C and
236K the value; for 149 the year's taxable salary) in rupees. `atl` is
`True` if the person is on the list and is required. `late_filer=True`
is for a person on the list who filed late; it changes the rate only
where the year has a late-filer rate (236C and 236K in 2025 and 2026).
`return_on_investment` is for 151 sukuk held by an individual or AOP:
the holder's return on investment, which decides the case (more than Rs 1
million: `sukuk-individual-above-1m`; less than Rs 1 million:
`sukuk-individual-below-1m`); it defaults to `amount`. The law gives
no rate for exactly Rs 1 million, so that, or a case that does not fit
the return, gives `None`. `resident` is for 154B: the rate is the
same, but it decides whether the tax is a minimum tax (resident) or a
final tax (non-resident without a permanent establishment in Pakistan),
given in `tax_nature`.
`tax_year` (e.g. `2027`) takes precedence over `date`. All of them
may also be passed as one `dict` with the npm package's camelCase keys.

The rate for a person not on the list follows each case's own rule in the
Tenth Schedule: usually double, but a fixed rate (236C, and 151 in 2025),
its own value bands (236K), or none (149; 231AB applies only to them).
The rate applies to the whole amount (236C and 236K value bands are not
marginal), and the tax is rounded to the nearest rupee (section 219; for
149, the salaried rate table is computed exactly and rounded once).
Where FBR's card and the Ordinance differ, the Ordinance is used and
`statute_override` says so. For 231AB, pass the day's total of all cash
withdrawals: nothing is collected up to Rs 50,000. For 150 mutual fund
dividends received by a company, the debt part is
`mutual-fund-debt-part-company` (29%).

This is an estimate from the rate card, not tax advice: exemptions,
reduced-rate certificates, adjustable or final status and the many cases
not listed here are not applied. Returns the rate, tax and references
({@link Withholding}), or `None` for an unknown section, case or tax
year, an invalid amount, or a missing `atl`. Never raises.

```python
>>> calculate_withholding(section="236K", amount=60_000_000, atl=False, tax_year=2027).rate
14.5
>>> calculate_withholding(section="231AB", amount=80_000, atl=False, tax_year=2027).tax
640
>>> calculate_withholding(
...     section="151", sub_type="bank-deposit", amount=10_000, atl=True, tax_year=2027
... ).tax
2000
```

entries.name: get_zakat_nisab
entries.doc:
The nisab for compulsory Zakat deduction at source in Pakistan for a
Zakat year, as notified by the Administrator-General Zakat (Ministry of
Poverty Alleviation & Social Safety) and conveyed to banks by SBP, Zakat
years 1433 to 1447 AH (2012-2026).

Give the year with `zakat_year` (`1447`, `"1447"` or the
notification's `"1446-47"`) or a `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD` or a
`datetime.date`); `zakat_year` takes precedence. They may also be
passed as a `dict`, `{"zakatYear": 1447}` or `{"date": ...}`, as in
the npm package. A Zakat year starts on 1 Ramazan. Where its Gregorian
date is confirmed (`valuation_date`, 2026 so far), that date is used.
Otherwise only the two likely days the notification gives are known, and
for a date on the first of them the year is unknown and the result is
`None`.

This is the nisab for deduction from savings and similar bank accounts
under the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980, not a religious ruling on
personal Zakat.

Returns the year's nisab, dates and sources ({@link ZakatNisab}), or
`None` for a year that is not covered, an invalid query or an
ambiguous date. Never raises.

```python
>>> get_zakat_nisab(zakat_year=1447).nisab
503529
>>> get_zakat_nisab(zakat_year="1445-46").zakat_year
1446
>>> get_zakat_nisab(date="2025-06-01").nisab
179689
```

entries.name: get_zakat_years
entries.doc:
Every notified Zakat year that {@link get_zakat_nisab} covers, as Hijri
years, oldest first.

```python
>>> get_zakat_years()[0]
1433
```

entries.name: zakat_deduction
entries.signature:
def zakat_deduction(
    input: Any = None,
    *,
    balance: Any = None,
    zakat_year: Any = None,
    date: Any = None,
    exempt: Any = False,
) -> Optional[ZakatDeduction]
entries.doc:
Zakat deducted at source from one account on the valuation date (1
Ramazan): 2.5% of the whole balance, rounded to the nearest rupee (First
Schedule, Note 2), when it is at or above that year's nisab, and nothing
when it is below or the holder has a valid exemption declaration (Form
CZ-50, `exempt=True`).

`exempt=True` means the declaration was filed with the bank at least 30
days before the valuation date, sworn before a magistrate, oath
commissioner, notary public or other person authorised to administer
oaths, in the presence of two witnesses (Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980,
s. 1(3), proviso (a)). The library does not check the declaration.

A balance exactly equal to the nisab is deducted, as the notifications
say ("Rs. 503,529/- or above" in 2026). The Ordinance's First Schedule
says no deduction where the balance "does not exceed" the nisab, which
would not deduct it; the library follows the notifications, which banks
apply.

`balance` is the account balance in rupees at the start of the
valuation date (0 to 1 trillion, at most 2 decimals count). The year is
given by `zakat_year` or `date`, as in {@link get_zakat_nisab}. All of
them may also be passed as one `dict` with the npm package's keys:
`{"balance": 600000, "zakatYear": 1447, "exempt": True}`.

It applies to the accounts the Ordinance subjects to deduction at source:
savings, profit-and-loss sharing and similar accounts (asset code 101).
Current accounts and foreign currency accounts are not deducted. It is
not a religious ruling on how much Zakat a person owes.

Returns the deduction and its source ({@link ZakatDeduction}), or
`None` for an invalid balance, a year that is not covered, or an
ambiguous date. Never raises.

```python
>>> zakat_deduction(balance=600000, zakat_year=1447).zakat
15000
>>> zakat_deduction(balance=600000, zakat_year=1447, exempt=True).reason
'exempt'
```
